task.description:
WF-03 Step 1 ISSUE-FIXER (.claude/agents/issue-fixer.md): diagnose and DESIGN the fix for RC-E, the diag-block interleave flake of test/scripts/test_parallel_watchdog_diag_test.exs "huge partition log: diagnostics stay bounded and respect the 300-column cap" (queue id pending from letflow-2; GH body will say RC-E MAJOR). Branch feature/WF03-RCEDIAGINTERLEAVE-20261013 is off origin/main 3a4ca1200 (Q-1053 / PR #2440 merged). LOCAL ONLY: do not push, do not open a PR; commit locally.

Evidence (three CI occurrences, same symptom, none reproduced locally yet): runs 38293810774 attempt 1 (job 114960028887, shard 1/3 partition 3), 38301751106 attempt 1 (job 114986157916), 38334100544 (shard 2/3 partition 5, job 115074477292; red on PR #2440, green on rerun). Assertion text of the last: "DIAG line wider than cap (399): test_parallel: DIAG partition 1:   P1-199974-LLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLtest_parallel: DIAG partition 2:   P2-199962-LLLL..." i.e. the DIAG block of partition 1 was cut mid-line (after 19 of the 300 L) and the next partition's DIAG lines continued on the same physical line. All three partitions use TEST_PARALLEL_PARTITION_TIMEOUT_S=2 so their watchdog subshells fire together; host loadavg 9-10 on 4 cores; CI stderr of the runner is a pipe/file captured by the ExUnit test (System.cmd or Port). The emitting function is test_parallel_watchdog_diag in scripts/test_parallel.sh (about lines 790-825): it writes `echo`, then `tail -n 40 log | cut -c1-300 | sed "s/^/pfx  /"` inside `{ ... } >&2`, plus a host block under a mkdir lock. Gathering: `gh api repos/tvolodi/letflow/actions/jobs/<job id>/logs` (job ids above) for the exact interleave bytes.

Tasks: (1) Establish the mechanism with an experiment, not by speculation: why can two watchdog blocks interleave MID-LINE? Candidates: sed/cut stdio buffering flushing partial lines when the output is a pipe or file and >PIPE_BUF/buffer size, two writers sharing one open file description without O_APPEND, the harness reading with a line splitter. Reproduce deterministically at script level (a standalone bash experiment with two concurrent emitters writing into a pipe read by a slow reader, and into a file; vary `cut`/`sed` with `stdbuf`, 400-column lines x 40, bash 5.2 linux in a container is fine if the host cannot reproduce; the host is Windows git-bash, a `docker run bash:5.2` or ubuntu container works; throwaway, remove after). Report rates (N runs, loaded with busy loops) for the unfixed emitter. (2) Design the fix: each partition's DIAG block must reach stderr as ONE uninterleaved unit, with a bounded and never-blocking mechanism (e.g. assemble the block into a variable/temp file first and emit it with a single write, serialised by a bounded mkdir lock with stale-lock/timeout fallback so a dead holder can never block the watchdog or the TERM path). State exactly what is atomic and why. Keep the 300-column cap, the 40-line tail, the host block, the final marker "approx tests finished" line, and the exit behaviour unchanged. (3) Regression test design: a deterministic test that fails on the unfixed script (e.g. BASH_ENV shim or a stub that makes the emission slow/forced concurrent) and passes on the fix, not a wall-clock window; plus mutants. Reuse test/support/test_parallel_capture.ex and the shim conventions of test/scripts/test_parallel_race_regression_test.exs. (4) Baseline plan: stress loop of the diag test file on UNMODIFIED main under the same load for the stable "0 failures" claim (loop capped to ~40 min total, under the machine mutex, one BEAM, >=4 GB free RAM waiter floor): propose the loop shape and iteration count (the CI rate is roughly 1 in 5 runs on loaded shards). (5) Anything else in test_parallel.sh that emits multi-line output from concurrent subshells (WARNING lines, partition summary) and could interleave the same way.

Rules: no application code edits in this step (design only; experiments in the scratchpad dir or a container), foreground only (no Monitors), machine mutex for any BEAM: L=/c/Users/tvolo/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/mixlock; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$L")"; until mkdir "$L" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 20; done; trap 'rmdir "$L" 2>/dev/null' EXIT; cd /c/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow && LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5499 MIX_ENV=test <ONE mix invocation>. Result into your handoff (COMPLETED, result.status PASS/FAIL, no BOM, LF, artifacts_out under result, no self-reference); commit locally on this branch, no push. Message ends: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>.

result.summary:
RC-E CONFIRMED BY EXPERIMENT. Mechanism: in test_parallel_watchdog_diag the 40-line tail goes through `tail | cut | sed`; sed is the OUTPUT stage and writes straight to the shared stderr pipe. sed is a stdio program: with a pipe/file as stdout it is fully buffered (glibc, 4096 B for a pipe) and emits its output in 4096-byte write(2)s at ARBITRARY byte offsets, i.e. mid-line. A huge-case DIAG block is 40 lines x (35 prefix + 300 cut + LF = 336 B) = ~13.4 KB, so each partition's sed does 3-4 separate writes. Three watchdog subshells (all TIMEOUT_S=2) run their pipelines concurrently, so another partition's 4096-byte chunk lands between two chunks of this partition's block. Each write(2) <= PIPE_BUF is atomic, but chunks are not line-aligned, so the reader sees `P3-199974-` + 19 L, then the other partition's chunk starting `test_parallel: DIAG partition 2:`. EXACT-OFFSET PROOF from the CI logs (jobs 114960028887 and 114986157916 fetched via gh api; the third job's log did not contain the text): the cut is always after `P<n>-199974-` + 19 `L`; line 199974 is the 13th tail line (first tail line is P-199962) so it starts at 12*336 = 4032 bytes into sed's output, and 35+10+19 = 64 bytes into it => 4032+64 = 4096 exactly. The `echo` header is a separate bash builtin write and does not shift sed's buffer. Only the `huge` case can show it: the `marked` case's block is < 4096 B, so sed flushes once at exit (one atomic write) - which is why only 'huge partition log' flakes.

EXPERIMENT (ubuntu:22.04 container, bash 5.1.16, 16 cores with 32 busy loops, emitter body copied verbatim from the script, 3 concurrent emitters, 200k-line 400-col logs, N=100 per cell; midline_bad = any line holding two DIAG prefixes, any line > 340 cols, or wrong line count): UNFIXED emitter: pipe reader 8/100 mid-line corrupt, slow reader (512 B per 10 ms) 8/100, shared file 5/100; whole-line interleave (harmless to existing assertions) 100/100 in all three. Reader speed does not matter (the 64 KB pipe absorbs the writes); load only widens the race. VARIANTS: `sed -u` removes mid-line cuts (0/100) but still interleaves whole lines 100/100 and gives no block guarantee; assembling in a bash variable and `printf '%s\n' "$blk" >&2` is STILL BROKEN: 6/100 (pipe) and 3/100 (file) mid-line, because the printf builtin goes through stdio and splits a >4 KB string into several write(2)s; assembling in a temp file and `cat "$f" >&2` (one 128 KB-buffer read, ONE write(2) for a <= ~14 KB block): 0/100 mid-line and 0/100 interleave on pipe, slow pipe and file; temp file + bounded mkdir lock + cat: 0/100 and 0/100 (pipe and file). DETERMINISTIC FORCING (validated): a `sed` shim first on PATH that, only for the invocation whose first arg starts `s/^/test_parallel: DIAG partition `, runs the real sed and re-emits its output in 1000-byte chunks in lock-step across partitions (file barrier, bounded) failed the unfixed emitter 5/5 and the temp-file+cat emitter 0/5. The Windows git-bash host was not used for reproduction (different pipe semantics from the Linux CI runner).

root_cause.function: test_parallel_watchdog_diag in scripts/test_parallel.sh (~lines 792-825): the `{ echo; tail|cut|sed; ...; } >&2` partition block, and the same hazard in the host block `{...} | cut -c1-300 | sed "s/^/${h}/"`
root_cause.broken_invariant: 'each partition's DIAG block reaches stderr as one uninterleaved unit' was never established: the block is emitted as several independent write(2)s from sed's non-line-aligned 4096 B stdio buffer onto a pipe shared by three concurrent watchdog subshells. Not a harness line-splitter problem and not an O_APPEND problem; the Elixir Port reads bytes in written order.
root_cause.why_tests_did_not_catch: Timing only: sed's chunk boundary straddles another partition's chunk when the three pipelines run within ms of each other (CI load makes that likely: ~5-8% per huge-case run measured). The existing assertions check per-line integrity, the ISS-1080 premise check only retries on a missing marker, not on a corrupted block.

fix_design.scope: scripts/test_parallel.sh only: test_parallel_watchdog_diag plus a new helper test_parallel_diag_emit. Unchanged: 300-col cut, 40-line tail, `approx tests finished` and `running for` lines, host block content and its diag-host.lock mkdir, WARNING lines, kill/TERM logic, exit codes.
fix_design.helper: test_parallel_diag_emit <blockfile>: (1) bounded lock: up to 30 iterations of `mkdir "$tmp_dir/diag-emit.lock" 2>/dev/null && { got=1; break; }; sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || sleep 1` (~3 s hard cap by iteration count; never waits on the holder); (2) `cat -- "$blockfile" >&2 || true` (ONE write(2)); (3) `[ "$got" = 1 ] && rmdir "$tmp_dir/diag-emit.lock" 2>/dev/null`; (4) `rm -f -- "$blockfile"`; always `return 0`. If the lock is not obtained in the bound (holder killed between mkdir and rmdir by the Step-3 group kill, or kill -9) it emits anyway: still one write(2), so a stale lock degrades to 'single write' and costs <= ~3 s before TERM, never a hang. No stale-age logic needed: the lock lives in the run's own $tmp_dir and is gone with the run.
fix_design.watchdog_function: Assemble OUTSIDE the lock into a temp file: `blk="$tmp_dir/diag-block-$idx.txt"; { echo header; tail -n 40 "$log" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-300 | sed "s/^/${pfx}  /"; k=...; echo approx; now/start; echo running; } > "$blk" 2>/dev/null || true; test_parallel_diag_emit "$blk"`. tail/cut/sed/grep now write to a regular file so sed's 4096 B chunking is harmless; the only interleave exposure is the single emit write. Host block (inside the existing diag-host.lock winner): same pattern via "$tmp_dir/diag-host-block.txt" and the same helper. Keep every existing `|| true` and the test_parallel_diag_t timeouts.
fix_design.what_is_atomic_and_why: Atomic unit = one cat write(2) of a <= ~14 KB regular file (40*336 B + 3 short lines; cat buffer 128 KB). On Linux pipe_write holds the pipe mutex for the whole write unless the 64 KB pipe is full (3 blocks < 45 KB), and a regular file's shared f_pos is advanced under the f_pos lock; independently, the mkdir lock (POSIX-atomic) makes the script's own emits mutually exclusive. Single write prevents mid-line cuts; lock is defence in depth. Not atomic vs a different writer such as another partition's WARNING echo: that is one line < PIPE_BUF and lands BETWEEN blocks, never inside. Rejected: printf of a big variable (measured 3-6% mid-line), sed -u (whole-line interleave), stdbuf (no effect on 3-writer interleave), flock (absent on default git-bash/macOS).
fix_design.cost: Lock hold time = one cat (<1 ms); one <= 14 KB temp file per partition, removed after emit.

regression_test_design.file: test/scripts/test_parallel_watchdog_diag_test.exs: new tests reusing run_script/3, write_stubs/1 (add `sed`, `mkdir`, `rmdir` shims in stubbin next to mix/psql, REAL_PATH via env), the `huge` stub mode, run_until_premise/huge_premise?, TestParallelCapture.with_context; conventions of test_parallel_race_regression_test.exs (stubs first on PATH, bookkeeping logs under tmp for the capture).
regression_test_design.test_1_block_integrity_forced_concurrenc: huge mode with env STUB_SED_CHUNK=1000 and STUB_BARRIER=<tmp>/barrier. sed shim: `case "$1" in 's/^/test_parallel: DIAG partition '*) ;; *) PATH="$REAL_PATH" exec sed "$@" ;; esac`; part=${1#s/^/test_parallel: DIAG partition }; part=${part%%:*}; pipe real sed through `while IFS= read -r -d '' -N "$STUB_SED_CHUNK" c || [ -n "$c" ]; do k=$((k+1)); : > "$STUB_BARRIER/$part.$k"; wait (<= 100 x sleep 0.05) until >= 3 files end in .$k; printf '%s' "$c"; c=; done`. Chunks of the three partitions are then emitted round-robin: the unfixed emitter is cut mid-line and adjacent to foreign text on EVERY run (validated 5/5 red), the fix writes the chunks into the temp file and one cat re-assembles them (validated 0/5 red). Bounded barrier => a fix that assembles under the lock only slows down, never deadlocks. Assertions (helper assert_blocks_intact): (a) no output line contains two `test_parallel: DIAG` occurrences; (b) every line starting `test_parallel: DIAG partition N: ` has <= byte_size(pfx(N)) + 2 + 300 bytes; (c) for each N the lines starting with pfx(N) form ONE contiguous run (no foreign line inside), first = `last 40 lines of` header, last = `running for ...`; (d) exactly 43 lines per block (header + 40 tail + approx + running); (e) exactly one host block, contiguous. Non-vacuity: assert >= 3 barrier files `*.1` exist so a renamed prefix cannot make the test green. Premise via run_until_premise + huge_premise?/1.
regression_test_design.test_2_stale_lock_bounded: mkdir shim: if "$*" contains diag-emit.lock, append `mkdir-denied` to $STUB_LOG and `exit 1` (dead holder that never releases), else exec real mkdir. huge mode, no sed shim. Assert: all 3 blocks present and intact, exit status unchanged (non-zero as in the existing huge test), returned within the limit (the three waits are concurrent, ~3 s), exactly 3 `mkdir-denied` entries.
regression_test_design.test_3_lock_released: rmdir shim logs `rmdir <path>` for diag-emit.lock then execs real rmdir; with the normal mkdir assert exactly 3 lock rmdirs.

baseline_plan.claim: Reproduce on UNMODIFIED main (3a4ca1200) with the real script, then same loop on the fix must show 0 failures.
baseline_plan.expected_rate: container: 5-8% per 3-way concurrent firing of the huge case under 2x oversubscription; CI ~1 in 5 shard runs. P(0 failures in N at p=0.06) = 0.94^N: N=40 -> 8%, N=50 -> 4.5%. Baseline N=40 as reproduction check (expect 1-4 failures); fix N=50 for the stable-0-failures claim.
baseline_plan.loop_shape: Under the machine mutex L=/c/Users/tvolo/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/mixlock (until mkdir; sleep 20; trap rmdir EXIT), >=4 GB free RAM waiter floor, ONE mix invocation at a time, foreground polling only. Chunked counting loop because --repeat-until-failure stops at the first failure: `for c in 1..5: LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5499 MIX_ENV=test mix test test/scripts/test_parallel_watchdog_diag_test.exs --only line:<huge test line> --repeat-until-failure 10`, record per chunk the completed repetitions and whether it failed; each chunk = one BEAM boot (~15 s) + <=10 huge-case runs (est. 8-12 s each: 3x awk of 200k lines + 2 s watchdog + 1 s grace) => ~2 min per chunk, ~10 min per 50 runs (ESTIMATE: the mutex was held by another session when a timing run was attempted, so per-iteration cost is not measured). Total cap 40 min; report actual repetitions and failures. Background load: 2x ncores `while :; do :; done` loops (killed in the trap) to approximate CI's loadavg/cores ~2.3. Record the failure text (expect cut after 19 L, 4096-aligned).
baseline_plan.caveat: Windows git-bash pipe/stdio semantics differ from the Linux CI runner; 0/40 on the host baseline does not exonerate - then rely on the deterministic sed-shim test plus the container numbers.

result.other_emitters: Checked every concurrent subshell/background job in scripts/test_parallel.sh: line 592 create/migrate -> create-N.log (file), 758 connection sampler -> a file, 842 mix test -> partition-N.log (file), 857-870 watchdog. The only concurrent stderr emitters are the watchdog's two WARNING `echo ... >&2` lines (one line each, one write(2) < PIPE_BUF => cannot be cut, may land between DIAG blocks, which the fix assumes) and the partition DIAG block + host DIAG block (the defect). The summary/WARNING lines at ~997-1017 run in the main shell after all watchdogs are reaped. The host block has the same `| cut | sed` hazard (usually < 4096 B, not guaranteed: ps/df output) and runs while other watchdogs still emit, so it must use the same helper; test_1 assertion (e) only exercises that if a `df` shim pads the host output > 4096 B (optional STUB_HOST_PAD). No change needed in test/support/test_parallel_capture.ex.
